questions.q: Taxus wallichiana Zucc (Himalayan yew) is a medicinal plant found in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh Key Points

The Himalayan Yew :

• The Himalayan Yew (Taxus wallachiana) is a medicinal plant found in various parts of Himachal Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh.

• The plant holds an important place in traditional medicine and its products are used by the local populations for treating common infections.

• A chemical compound called ‘taxol’ is extracted from the bark, needles, twigs and roots of this tree, and it has been successfully used to treat some cancers – the drug is now the biggest selling anti-cancer drug in the world.

• The species is under great threat due to over-exploitation.

• In the last decade, thousands of yew trees have dried up in various parts of Himachal Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh.

• Yew has undergone a recent, range-wide population decline of at least 50% as per IUCN.

• Due to the illegal cutting of plant parts and other anthropogenic pressures, Himalayan yew is endangered, and threatened with extinction, in Himalaya.

• Throughout its range in the western Himalayas, it is declining in response to a range of threats.

• In Afghanistan, up to 50% of the forests where it occurs have been destroyed or heavily logged (UNEP 2003) over the last 30 years.

• In northwest India and western Nepal, exploitation associated with Taxol production has led to a national decline of up to 90% in Taxus populations throughout the country.

• Also, in other countries such as Pakistan, overexploitation for fuel, fodder, and medicinal use has led to a significant decline.

• The decline is continuing and while the causes are largely understood, in many areas they will not be reversible. On this basis, an assessment of Endangered is warranted.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
options: Mitochondria: Power house of the cell
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nucleus: Lipid metabolism.

Key Points

• The nucleus is the control center of the cell, storing the cell's DNA and coordinating cellular activities such as growth, metabolism, and reproduction.

• Lipid metabolism is primarily associated with the smooth endoplasmic reticulum and not the nucleus.

• The nucleus is responsible for the transcription of DNA to mRNA, which is then translated into proteins by ribosomes.

• The nucleus also contains the nucleolus, which is involved in ribosome synthesis and assembly.

Additional Information

• Lysosomes:

• Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles that contain enzymes to break down biomolecules.

• They are often referred to as the "suicidal bags" of the cell because they can digest cellular components when the cell is damaged.

• They play a key role in the degradation and recycling of cellular waste, cellular signaling, and energy metabolism.

• Mitochondria:

• Mitochondria are known as the "powerhouses of the cell" because they generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.

• They are involved in other processes such as signaling, cellular differentiation, and cell death, as well as the control of the cell cycle and cell growth.

• Mitochondria have their own DNA and are thought to have originated from ancestral prokaryotes through endosymbiosis.

• Ribosomes:

• Ribosomes are the molecular machines responsible for protein synthesis.

• They translate messenger RNA (mRNA) into amino acid sequences to build proteins.

• Ribosomes can be found floating freely in the cytoplasm or bound to the endoplasmic reticulum, forming the rough ER.

• They are made up of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins and consist of two subunits, a large and a small one.

questions.q: Which of the following battles is considered the formal beginning of the British Raj in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Battle of Plassey.

Key Points

• The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757, in the eastern part of India.

• This battle marked the beginning of British colonial rule in India.

• It was fought between the British East India Company and the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj ud-Daulah.

• The British victory in this battle was largely due to the betrayal of Nawab's commander, Mir Jafar, who sided with the British.

Additional Information

• First Carnatic War

• The First Carnatic War (1746-1748) was fought between the British and the French in India.

• It was mainly a result of the War of Austrian Succession in Europe.

• The war ended with the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle in 1748, resulting in a status quo ante bellum.

• Battle of Wandiwash

• The Battle of Wandiwash was fought on 22 January 1760 between the British and the French.

• The British, under Sir Eyre Coote, decisively defeated the French forces.

• This battle marked the end of French colonial ambitions in India.

• Battle of Buxar

• The Battle of Buxar was fought on 22 October 1764 between the British East India Company and the combined forces of the Nawab of Bengal, Nawab of Awadh, and the Mughal Emperor.

• The British victory established their supremacy in the eastern parts of India.

• This battle was crucial for the British as it consolidated their power after the Battle of Plassey.

questions.q: Which of the following Indian states has the least number of operational airports as of 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mizoram.

Key Points

• Mizoram is a state in Northeast India, known for its scenic beauty and cultural heritage.

• As of 2022, Mizoram has only one operational airport, which is Lengpui Airport.

• Lengpui Airport is located near Aizawl, the capital city of Mizoram, and is the primary airport serving the state.

• Due to the state's hilly terrain and lower population density, the development of multiple airports has been limited.

Additional Information

• Operational Airports in India:

• India has a network of airports spread across its vast geography, including both international and domestic airports.

• The Airports Authority of India (AAI) is responsible for the development, maintenance, and management of civil aviation infrastructure in the country.

• As of 2022, some states like Maharashtra and Karnataka have multiple operational airports due to their larger land area and higher population density.

• Lengpui Airport:

• Lengpui Airport is the only operational airport in Mizoram and serves as the main gateway to the state.

• It is situated approximately 32 km from Aizawl, the state capital.

• The airport is equipped to handle both domestic flights and is known for its picturesque approach due to the surrounding hills.

• Lengpui Airport was inaugurated in 1998 and has since been a crucial part of Mizoram's connectivity.

• Challenges in Airport Development in Hilly Regions:

• Constructing and maintaining airports in hilly terrains like Mizoram presents unique challenges, including difficult topography and limited flat land availability.

• High construction costs and environmental concerns also play significant roles in limiting the number of airports.

• However, such regions can benefit greatly from air connectivity in terms of tourism and economic development.

• Importance of Air Connectivity:

• Air connectivity is crucial for the socio-economic development of any region, providing faster and more efficient transportation options.

• It facilitates trade, tourism, and cultural exchange, contributing to the overall growth of the region.

• For states like Mizoram, with challenging road infrastructure, air connectivity becomes even more important.

questions.q: Who among the following, while praising the amending feature of the Indian Constitution said that 'This variety in the amending process is wise but is rarely found'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is K C Wheare.

Key Points

• K C Wheare was a distinguished constitutional scholar known for his work on federalism and constitutional law.

• He praised the Indian Constitution's amending process for its variety and flexibility, which he considered wise and unique.

• Wheare emphasized that such variety in the amending process is rare among the world's constitutions.

• His observations highlight the robustness and adaptability of the Indian Constitution in accommodating changes.

Additional Information

• Granville Austin

• Granville Austin was an American historian who studied the Indian Constitution extensively.

• He is known for his seminal work, "The Indian Constitution: Cornerstone of a Nation," which examines the making and functioning of the Indian Constitution.

• Austin's work is highly regarded for its in-depth analysis and insight into the Indian constitutional process.

• Ivor Jennings

• Sir Ivor Jennings was a British lawyer and academic who made significant contributions to the study of constitutional law.

• He was involved in the drafting of several constitutions in the Commonwealth countries, including India.

• Jennings emphasized the importance of conventions and practices in the functioning of a constitution.

• HM Seervai

• H.M. Seervai was a prominent Indian jurist and constitutional expert.

• He authored the influential book "Constitutional Law of India," which is a comprehensive commentary on the Indian Constitution.

• Seervai's work is widely cited in legal circles and has greatly contributed to the understanding of the Indian constitutional law.

• Amending Process in the Indian Constitution

• The Indian Constitution provides a detailed procedure for its amendment in Part XX, Article 368.

• The amending process is categorized into three types: simple majority, special majority, and special majority with ratification by states.

• This flexibility allows the Constitution to be both rigid and flexible, accommodating necessary changes while maintaining stability.

• Amendments require different levels of parliamentary support and, in some cases, ratification by state legislatures, ensuring a broad consensus.

questions.q: Which of the following famous Indian athletes won the Zurich Diamond League final 2022 in September 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Neeraj Chopra.

Key Points

• Neeraj Chopra is an Indian track and field athlete who competes in the javelin throw.

• He created history by becoming the first Indian to win a gold medal in athletics at the Olympic Games when he won the men's javelin throw at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.

• On 8th September 2022, Neeraj Chopra became the first Indian to win the Zurich Diamond League final with a throw of 88.44 meters.

• He has consistently performed well in international competitions, bringing laurels to India in the field of athletics.

Important Points

• Zurich Diamond League

• The Diamond League is an annual series of elite track and field athletic competitions comprising fourteen of the best invitational athletics meetings.

• It was founded in 2010, and the Zurich meeting is one of the most prestigious events in this series.

• Athletes accumulate points at each Diamond League meet and the top performers in each event compete in the final, where the winner is crowned the Diamond League champion.

• Javelin Throw

• Javelin throw is a track and field event where the javelin, a spear about 2.5 meters in length, is thrown.

• The objective is to throw the javelin as far as possible; the athlete with the longest valid throw wins.

• It has been a part of the modern Olympic Games since its inception for men in 1908 and for women in 1932.

• Neeraj Chopra's Career Highlights

• Neeraj Chopra won the gold medal at the 2018 Commonwealth Games and the 2018 Asian Games, where he also set a new Indian national record.

• He made his mark internationally by becoming the World Junior Champion in 2016.

• He is also the first Indian to win a Diamond League title, which he achieved in August 2022 in Lausanne before winning the Zurich final.

questions.q: How many chambers are there in the heart of fishes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2.

Key Points

• Fishes have a two-chambered heart consisting of one atrium and one ventricle.

• The blood flows in a single circuit, from the heart to the gills for oxygenation and then to the rest of the body.

• The two-chambered heart is efficient for the aquatic life of fishes, supporting their metabolism and oxygen needs.

• Having a two-chambered heart is a characteristic feature of most fish species.

Additional Information

• Chambers of the Heart

• Atrium: The atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body and sends it to the ventricle.

• Ventricle: The ventricle pumps the deoxygenated blood to the gills for oxygenation.

• Circulatory System in Fishes

• Fishes have a single circulatory system, meaning blood passes through the heart only once during each complete circuit of the body.

• After oxygenation in the gills, the oxygen-rich blood is delivered directly to the tissues without returning to the heart.

• This system is different from mammals and birds, which have a double circulatory system.

• Gills

• Gills are the respiratory organs in fishes that allow them to extract oxygen from water.

• Blood flows through the gill filaments where gas exchange occurs – carbon dioxide is released into the water and oxygen is absorbed.

• Adaptations

• The two-chambered heart and single circulatory system are highly adapted to an aquatic environment where oxygen levels can vary.

• These adaptations ensure efficient oxygen delivery to support the metabolism and activity levels of fishes.

questions.q: What is the unit of measurement for optical power of the lens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Diopter.

Key Points

• The diopter (D) is the unit of measurement for the optical power of a lens or curved mirror.

• It is defined as the reciprocal of the focal length (f) measured in meters (i.e., D = 1/f).

• A lens with a focal length of 1 meter has an optical power of 1 diopter.

• Lenses with positive diopters are converging lenses, while those with negative diopters are diverging lenses.

Additional Information

• Optical Power:

• Optical power, also known as lens power, is the degree to which a lens converges or diverges light.

• It is an important concept in optics and is essential in the design of optical systems such as glasses, cameras, and telescopes.

• Focal Length:

• The focal length of a lens is the distance from the lens at which parallel rays of light converge to a single point.

• It determines the magnifying power of the lens and is crucial in the formation of clear images.

• Converging and Diverging Lenses:

• Converging lenses (positive diopters) focus light to a point and are used in applications like magnifying glasses and corrective lenses for hyperopia (farsightedness).

• Diverging lenses (negative diopters) spread light outwards and are used in devices like peepholes and corrective lenses for myopia (nearsightedness).

questions.q: Who among the following was the last sultan of Delhi sultanate?

• The battle marked the end of the Delhi Sultanate and the beginning of the Mughal Empire in India.

• Babur's use of innovative military tactics and artillery was instrumental in his victory.

• This battle is considered one of the most significant events in Indian history as it led to the establishment of Mughal rule, which lasted for over three centuries.

• Mughal Empire

• The Mughal Empire was an empire that controlled large parts of the Indian subcontinent from the early 16th to the mid-19th century.

• It was founded by Babur, a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan, after his victory in the First Battle of Panipat.

• The Mughal Empire is known for its rich cultural contributions, including significant developments in art, architecture, and cuisine.

questions.q: In the context of water bodies, Neap Tides occur:
options: when the earth, moon and sun line up in a straight line
when the sun and moon are on the opposite sides
when there is so much interference by continents
when the sun and moon are at right angles to each other
questions.solution:
The correct answer is when the sun and moon are at right angles to each other.

Key Points

• Neap tides occur when the gravitational forces of the moon and the sun are perpendicular to one another with respect to the Earth.

• These tides are characterized by the least difference between high and low tide levels, making them weaker compared to spring tides.

• Neap tides occur during the first and third quarters of the moon phase, approximately every two weeks.

• During neap tides, the tidal range is reduced because the sun's gravitational pull partially cancels out the moon's gravitational pull on the Earth's oceans.

Additional Information

• Spring Tides

• Spring tides occur when the Earth, moon, and sun are aligned, leading to the highest high tides and the lowest low tides.

• This alignment occurs during full moon and new moon phases.

• The combined gravitational force of the moon and sun leads to a greater tidal range.

• Gravitational Forces

• The gravitational forces of the moon and sun both affect the Earth's oceans, causing tides.

• The moon's gravitational force has a more significant impact due to its proximity to Earth.

• Tidal Range

• The tidal range is the difference in height between consecutive high and low tides.

• It varies depending on the alignment of the Earth, moon, and sun.

• Phases of the Moon

• The moon goes through different phases (new moon, first quarter, full moon, third quarter) as it orbits the Earth.

• These phases affect the gravitational pull on the Earth's oceans, leading to different types of tides.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India expressly provides that the President is eligible for re-election?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 57.

Key Points

• Article 57 of the Constitution of India states that a person who holds, or who has held, office as President shall, subject to the other provisions of this Constitution, be eligible for re-election to that office.

• This article ensures that there is no restriction on the number of times a person can be re-elected as President of India.

• The President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States.

• Article 57 is part of the chapter on the Executive, which is detailed in Part V of the Indian Constitution.

Additional Information

• Article 56

• Article 56 of the Constitution of India deals with the term of office of the President.

• According to this article, the President shall hold office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office.

• The President may resign from his office by writing under his hand addressed to the Vice-President of India.

• The President may, for violation of the Constitution, be removed from office by impeachment in the manner provided in Article 61.

• Article 58

• Article 58 lays down the qualifications for election as President of India.

• A person shall be eligible for election as President if he is a citizen of India, has completed the age of thirty-five years, and is qualified for election as a member of the House of the People.

• The person should not hold any office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State or under any local or other authority subject to the control of any of the said Governments.

• Article 59

• Article 59 deals with the conditions of the President's office.

• The President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State, and if a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State be elected President, he shall be deemed to have vacated his seat in that House on the date on which he enters upon his office as President.

• The President shall not hold any other office of profit.

• The President shall be entitled to such emoluments, allowances, and privileges as may be determined by Parliament by law and, until provision in that behalf is so made, such emoluments, allowances, and privileges as are specified in the Second Schedule.

• The emoluments and allowances of the President shall not be diminished during his term of office.

questions.q: The salary of a worker is first increased by 25%, then it is decreased by 12%. The percentage change in his salary is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net percentage change formula: a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, a = +25% (increase) and b = −12% (decrease).

⇒ Net change = 25 − 12 + (25 × −12) ÷ 100

⇒ Net change = 13 − 3 = +10%

Positive sign indicates an overall increase.

∴ The correct answer is 10% increase.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial salary increase = 25%

Subsequent salary decrease = 12%



Calculations:

Let the initial salary of the worker be 100.

⇒ Salary after 25% increase = 100 + (25 ÷ 100 × 100) = 125

⇒ Decrease amount = 12% of 125 = (12 ÷ 100) × 125 = 15

⇒ Final salary = 125 − 15 = 110

⇒ Overall change = Final salary − Initial salary = 110 − 100 = +10

⇒ Percentage change = (10 ÷ 100) × 100% = 10% increase

∴ The correct answer is 10% increase.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is subjected to successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the net change can be found using the formula: Net % = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Multiplying Factor Method

For successive changes, the final value can be directly calculated as: Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± f₁) × (1 ± f₂), where f represents the fractional equivalent of the percentage.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100. A positive result denotes an increase, while a negative result indicates a decrease.

questions.q: Pipe A usually fills a tank in 6 hours. But due to a leak at the bottom of the tank, it takes extra 2 hours to fill the tank. If the tank is full, then how much time will it take to get emptied due to the leak?

Shortcut Trick

If a pipe fills a tank in x hours and due to a leak it takes y hours to fill, the leak alone can empty the tank in (x × y) ÷ (y − x) hours.

Here, x = 6 hours and y = 6 + 2 = 8 hours.

Required time = (6 × 8) ÷ (8 − 6) = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 24 hours.

questions.q: Find the area of a square, one of whose diagonals is 4.8 m long.

Shortcut Trick

The area of a square can be directly calculated if the length of its diagonal is known.

Area of square = (Diagonal)² ÷ 2

Area = (4.8)² ÷ 2

∴ The correct answer is 11.52 m².

Alternate Method

Diagonal of a square = √2 × Side

Area of a square = (Side)²

⇒ Side = 4.8 ÷ √2 m

⇒ Area = (4.8 × 4.8) ÷ (√2 × √2)

⇒ Area = 23.04 ÷ 2

Additional Information

Perimeter of a Square

The perimeter is the total continuous length of the boundary of the square. It is calculated as P = 4 × Side.

Diagonal and Side Relation

A diagonal divides the square into two identical right-angled isosceles triangles. Applying Pythagoras theorem, the relationship formed is Diagonal = √2 × Side.

Circumcircle of a Square

questions.q: Which of the following numbers is divisible by both 2 and 5?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a number to be divisible by both 2 and 5, it must be divisible by their Lowest Common Multiple (LCM).

The LCM of 2 and 5 is 10.

A number is divisible by 10 if and only if its last digit is 0.

Looking at the given options, only 63840 has a last digit of 0.

∴ The correct answer is 63840.

Alternate Method

Given:

Numbers to check: 63840, 20792, 37915, 37254

Concept Used:

Divisibility by 2: The last digit must be an even number (0, 2, 4, 6, 8).

Divisibility by 5: The last digit must be 0 or 5.

Calculations:

⇒ For a number to be divisible by both 2 and 5, the last digit must satisfy both rules simultaneously.

⇒ The only digit that is even and also satisfies the rule of 5 is 0.

⇒ Option 1: 63840 ends with 0, hence it is divisible by both 2 and 5.

⇒ Option 2: 20792 ends with 2, so it is divisible by 2 but not by 5.

⇒ Option 3: 37915 ends with 5, so it is divisible by 5 but not by 2.

⇒ Option 4: 37254 ends with 4, so it is divisible by 2 but not by 5.

∴ The correct answer is 63840.

Additional Information

Divisibility by 3 and 9

A number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of its individual digits is a multiple of 3 or 9 respectively.

Divisibility by 4 and 8

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits form a number divisible by 4. It is divisible by 8 if its last three digits form a number divisible by 8.

Divisibility by 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits in odd places and the sum of digits in even places is 0 or a multiple of 11.

Divisibility by Composite Numbers

To check divisibility by a composite number (like 6, 12, or 15), factorize it into co-prime factors. For example, a number is divisible by 6 if it is divisible by both 2 and 3.

Mean Proportional

In a right-angled triangle at B, the sum of acute angles ∠A and ∠C is 90°.

⇒ ∠C = 90° − ∠A

Taking cosine on both sides gives cos C = cos(90° − A).

Using the complementary angle identity cos(90° − θ) = sin θ, we directly get cos C = sin A.

Given sin A = 1/2, it follows that cos C = 1/2.

∴ The correct answer is 1/2.

Alternate Method

In ΔABC, ∠B = 90° and sin A = 1/2.

sin θ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse

cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

Calculations:

⇒ sin A = BC / AC = 1 / 2

⇒ Let BC = 1 unit and AC = 2 units.

⇒ By Pythagoras theorem, AB = √(AC² − BC²) = √(2² − 1²) = √3 units.

⇒ We need to find cos C.

⇒ In ΔABC, ∠C = 180° − (90° + 30°) = 60°

⇒ cos C = cos 60° = 1 / 2

∴ The correct answer is 1/2.

Additional Information

Complementary Angles in Trigonometry

If two angles A and B sum up to 90°, they are complementary. The trigonometric ratios shift exactly such that sin A = cos B, tan A = cot B, and sec A = cosec B.

Trigonometric Ratios for 30°, 60°, 90° Triangles

In a right-angled triangle with angles 30°-60°-90°, the sides are always in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2 respectively opposite to the angles.

For any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides. Formula: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base².

Shortcut Trick

The given expression follows the standard algebraic identity: (a³ − b³) ÷ (a² + ab + b²) = a − b

Here, a = 4.2 and b = 1.2

Simply calculate the difference: 4.2 − 1.2 = 3

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Given:

Expression: (4.2³ − 1.2³) ÷ (4.2² + 5.04 + 1.2²)

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

⇒ [(a − b)(a² + ab + b²)] ÷ (a² + ab + b²)

⇒ The common term (a² + ab + b²) in the numerator and denominator cancels out.

⇒ Remaining expression = a − b

⇒ Result = 4.2 − 1.2 = 3

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Additional Information

Sum of Cubes Identity

Similar to the difference of cubes, the sum of cubes formula is useful in simplifications: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²).

Another highly used algebraic identity in exams is a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).

questions.q: If 0.4x + 0.16y = 1.7 and 0.3x + 0.12y = 3.4, then which of the following is correct?

The system has infinitely many solutions.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For linear equations a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂, directly check their coefficient ratios.

Ratio of x-coefficients (a₁/a₂) = 0.4 ÷ 0.3 = 4/3

Ratio of y-coefficients (b₁/b₂) = 0.16 ÷ 0.12 = 4/3

Ratio of constants (c₁/c₂) = 1.7 ÷ 3.4 = 1/2

Since a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, the lines are parallel and never intersect.

∴ The correct answer is no solution.

Alternate Method

Given:

0.4x + 0.16y = 1.7

0.3x + 0.12y = 3.4

Formula Used:

For a system of linear equations a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂:

If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, the system represents parallel lines and has no solution.

Calculations:

⇒ To simplify, multiply the first equation by 100 to remove decimals:

⇒ 40x + 16y = 170

⇒ Multiply the second equation by 100:

⇒ 30x + 12y = 340

⇒ Now, compare the coefficients with standard form:

⇒ a₁ = 40, b₁ = 16, c₁ = 170

⇒ a₂ = 30, b₂ = 12, c₂ = 340

⇒ Find the ratio a₁/a₂ = 40 ÷ 30 = 4/3

⇒ Find the ratio b₁/b₂ = 16 ÷ 12 = 4/3

⇒ Find the ratio c₁/c₂ = 170 ÷ 340 = 1/2

⇒ We can observe that a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂

⇒ This means the equations represent distinct parallel lines, so they will never intersect.

∴ The correct answer is no solution.

Additional Information

Unique Solution (Intersecting Lines)

If a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂, the lines intersect at exactly one point, giving a single unique solution.

Infinitely Many Solutions (Coincident Lines)

If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂, the lines overlap entirely, resulting in infinitely many common points or solutions.

No Solution (Parallel Lines)

If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, the lines have the same slope but different intercepts, making them parallel with no point of intersection.

questions.q: The cost price of a bat is 75% of the marked price. Calculate the gain percentage after allowing a discount of 15%.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the Marked Price (MP) be 100 units.

Cost Price (CP) = 75% of 100 = 75 units.

Selling Price (SP) after 15% discount = 100 − 15 = 85 units.

Profit = SP − CP = 85 − 75 = 10 units.

Profit % = (10 ÷ 75) × 100 = 13.33%.

∴ The correct answer is 13.33%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Discount allowed = 15%



Formula Used:

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount %) ÷ 100

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let Marked Price (MP) = 100x

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = 75% of 100x = 75x

⇒ Discount = 15% of 100x = 15x

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 100x − 15x = 85x

⇒ Gain = SP − CP = 85x − 75x = 10x

⇒ Gain % = (10x ÷ 75x) × 100

⇒ Gain % = (2 ÷ 15) × 100 = 40 ÷ 3 = 13.33%

∴ The correct answer is 13.33%.

Additional Information

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) unless explicitly stated otherwise. Formula: SP = MP × (1 − D/100).

Direct Relation Between CP and MP

When Profit/Loss % and Discount % are given, the ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is given by: CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 ± Profit/Loss%).

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is calculated as: Equivalent Discount = a + b − (a × b)/100.

Alternate Method



Given:

Initial distance between policeman and thief = 200 m

Speed of policeman = 11 km/h

Speed of thief = 10 km/h

Time = 9 minutes

Formula Used:

Relative Speed (when moving in the same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Distance = Speed × Time

1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

Calculations:

⇒ Relative speed = 11 − 10 = 1 km/h

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 1 × (5/18) = 5/18 m/s

⇒ Time in seconds = 9 × 60 = 540 seconds

⇒ Distance covered by policeman relative to thief = Relative speed × Time

⇒ Relative distance = (5/18) × 540 = 5 × 30 = 150 m

⇒ Remaining distance between them = Initial distance − Relative distance

⇒ Remaining distance = 200 − 150 = 50 m

∴ The correct answer is 50 m.

Additional Information

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = S₁ + S₂.

Speed Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the speed value by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.q: The value of the expression (1.55² + 0.55² + 1.55 x 0.55) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify the form of the expression: a² + b² + ab, where a = 1.55 and b = 0.55.

Using the standard algebraic identity: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + b² + ab).

Here, a − b = 1.55 − 0.55 = 1.

Therefore, a² + b² + ab = a³ − b³ directly.

∴ The correct answer is 1.55³ − 0.55³.

Alternate Method

Given:

The expression: 1.55² + 0.55² + 1.55 × 0.55

Formula Used:

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

Calculation:

⇒ Let a = 1.55 and b = 0.55

⇒ The given expression takes the form: a² + b² + ab

⇒ Rearranging the formula for the difference of cubes, we get: a² + ab + b² = (a³ − b³) ÷ (a − b)

⇒ Find the value of the denominator: a − b = 1.55 − 0.55 = 1

⇒ Substitute the numerical values back into the rearranged formula:

⇒ 1.55² + 1.55 × 0.55 + 0.55² = (1.55³ − 0.55³) ÷ 1

⇒ 1.55² + 1.55 × 0.55 + 0.55² = 1.55³ − 0.55³

∴ The correct answer is 1.55³ − 0.55³.

Additional Information

Sum of Cubes Identity

The formula for the sum of cubes is a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²).

Difference of Squares

A fundamental algebraic identity is a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).

Perfect Square Trinomials

The expansion of squared binomials follows the identities (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².
